aurora/0.title: Data center moratorium and new data center rules
aurora/0.summary: Council adopted a moratorium on development applications that include a data center, directed staff to write data center regulations, and worked through development standards and a zoning use table change for data centers, ending in a public hearing in October.

aurora/1.title: Water rules on evaporative cooling, turf and water features
aurora/1.summary: Council passed Aurora Water ordinances on evaporative cooling and limits on new turf and ornamental water features, and set 2027 water rates and fees.

aurora/2.title: 2027 budget deliberations
aurora/2.summary: Council spent a day going department by department through the 2027 budget, service fees, pay tables and improvement district budgets.

aurora/3.title: Homeless services funding and the Regional Navigation Campus
aurora/3.summary: Council funded outdoor renovations at the Aurora Regional Navigation Campus and reviewed a slate of homeless services grant recommendations for emergency shelter, rapid rehousing and rental help.

aurora/4.title: Nine Mile Station redevelopment
aurora/4.summary: The Aurora Urban Renewal Authority amended the Point Crossing agreement and approved a redevelopment agreement for the Tempo at Nine Mile Station apartments.

aurora/5.title: Affordable housing ground lease with Mercy Housing
aurora/5.summary: Council approved a ground lease with Mercy Housing for an affordable housing project and assigned the city's private activity bonds to the Aurora Housing Authority.

aurora/6.title: Socioeconomic sales and services impact permit
aurora/6.summary: Council introduced an ordinance requiring an impact permit for certain sales and services businesses.

aurora/7.title: Support for Proposition 308
aurora/7.summary: Council took up a resolution supporting state ballot Proposition 308.

aurora/8.title: Oil and gas lease and advisory board
aurora/8.summary: Council considered an oil and gas lease and filled seats on the Oil and Gas Advisory Committee.

aurora/9.title: Police and fire union contracts
aurora/9.summary: Council approved 2027-2028 collective bargaining agreements with the firefighters' and police unions.

aurora/10.title: Regis Jesuit High comprehensive plan change
aurora/10.summary: Council held a public hearing on changing the comprehensive plan map for land near Regis Jesuit High north of East Arapahoe Road.
aurora/10.where: E Arapahoe Rd & S Olathe St

boulder-county/0.title: 2027 county budget and budget cuts
boulder-county/0.summary: Commissioners reviewed an efficiencies project and general fund budget reductions, heard department requests for 2027, and held a public hearing on the recommended budget ahead of adoption on December 8.

sources.body: Department and Office Requests 2027 Boulder County Budget
Department and Office Requests 2027 Boulder County Budget
Public Meeting on the 2027 Recommended Budgets

boulder-county/1.title: Xcel easements across county open space
boulder-county/1.summary: Commissioners held a public hearing on Xcel taking three permanent easements across about 1.38 acres of the Liley, Simi and Tommy Thompson open space properties for the 120th Street shoulder rebuild.

boulder-county/2.title: Affordable housing tax innovation fund and San Lazaro
boulder-county/2.summary: Commissioners discussed the Affordable and Attainable Housing Tax innovation fund and a letter of intent for funding at San Lazaro, and the housing authority held hearings on its 2027 plans.
boulder-county/2.where: San Lazaro mobile home park, countywide

sources.body: Boulder County Housing Authority Moving to Work Supplement to Annual Plan

boulder-county/3.title: Zero waste plan, fees and composting
boulder-county/3.summary: Public Works updated commissioners on the zero waste plan, including possible fees and composting.

boulder-county/4.title: Tucker Complex interim management
boulder-county/4.summary: Parks and Open Space proposed an interim management plan for the Tucker Complex.

boulder-county/5.title: Mental and behavioral health tax advisory committee
boulder-county/5.summary: Commissioners set up the advisory committee and bylaws for the mental and behavioral health tax.

boulder-county/6.title: Emergency services tax and grants
boulder-county/6.summary: Commissioners heard an update on the emergency services tax and its grant program.

boulder-county/7.title: Commissioners' town halls on the budget and disaster preparedness
boulder-county/7.summary: Commissioners held town halls in Superior on the 2027 budget and in Lafayette on disaster preparedness, taking residents' questions.

boulder-county/8.title: Public improvement district budgets
boulder-county/8.summary: Commissioners reviewed 2027 budgets for the Burgundy Park, Eldorado Springs, Gunbarrel, Homestead and Nederland EcoPass public improvement districts.

sources.body: Public Meeting on the 2027 Recommended Budgets

boulder/0.title: November ballot measures
boulder/0.summary: Council put several questions on the November 3 ballot, including general obligation bonds for recreation and safety projects, a vacancy excise tax on homes occupied 183 days a year or less, a charter right for firefighters to bargain collectively, and a wildfire resilience measure for open space.

boulder/1.title: Boulder Downtown Development Authority
boulder/1.summary: Council moved to ask downtown voters whether to form a Downtown Development Authority that could use tax increment financing for downtown projects.

boulder/2.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening
boulder/2.summary: Council worked on a wildfire home hardening hub and a review of every city wildfire program as a council priority project, alongside the open space wildfire ballot measure.

boulder/3.title: Local minimum wage increase
boulder/3.summary: Council held the second reading of an ordinance setting Boulder's local minimum wage.

boulder/4.title: 2027 budget
boulder/4.summary: Council held a study session on the 2027 recommended budget and then adopted budgets and mill levies for the downtown, University Hill and Boulder Junction improvement districts.
boulder/4.where: Citywide, Downtown, University Hill, Boulder Junction

boulder/5.title: Eminent domain for the 30th Street projects
boulder/5.summary: Council introduced ordinances allowing the city to buy or condemn land for the North 30th Street project and the South 30th Street multimodal improvements.

boulder/6.title: Annexation of Cherryvale Road and McSorley Lane properties
boulder/6.summary: Council took up a petition to annex about 5.4 acres at 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln. with rural residential zoning, setting a public hearing for November 12.

boulder/7.title: Affordable housing bonds for Boulder Housing Partners and Harvest34
boulder/7.summary: Council assigned $7.3 million in private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners for permanently affordable rentals and cleared housing revenue bonds for the Harvest34 project.

boulder/8.title: Arapahoe Avenue rezoning and Naropa campus redevelopment
boulder/8.summary: Council introduced a rezoning of 3.7 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Avenue to high-density residential, vacated part of Marine Street, and reviewed a site plan to redevelop the Naropa campus.

boulder/9.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update
boulder/9.summary: Council introduced the ordinance adopting the 2025 major ten-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.

boulder/10.title: Power reliability and resilience forum
boulder/10.summary: Council held a community forum on power reliability and resilience, a council priority project, and reviewed a concept plan to expand Xcel Energy's service center at 2655 N. 63rd Street.

boulder/11.title: Civic Area East Bookend redevelopment
boulder/11.summary: Council discussed a request for proposals for a development partner on the east end of the Civic Area.

boulder/12.title: Marijuana and liquor licensing changes
boulder/12.summary: Council updated the medical and recreational marijuana code and created expanded permits and a tax for spirits manufacturers.

boulder/13.title: Pedicab licenses
boulder/13.summary: Council created licenses and fees for pedicab companies and drivers.

boulder/14.title: Frasier senior campus expansion
boulder/14.summary: Council reviewed a site review amendment for Frasier to build a 55-foot, four-story, 96-unit independent living building with underground parking.

boulder/15.title: Landmark designations at 1004 Lincoln Place and 844-850 12th Street
boulder/15.summary: Council designated two properties as individual landmarks.

broomfield/0.title: Broomfield Town Square revocation hearing
broomfield/0.summary: Two council members asked council to start a revocation hearing for the Broomfield Town Square site development plan, and council took up a notice to show cause in October.

broomfield/1.title: 2027 operating and capital budgets
broomfield/1.summary: Council heard economic and fiscal updates, the long-range financial plan and department budget presentations, then held a public hearing on the 2027 operating and capital budgets.

broomfield/2.title: Lodging tax and Xcel franchise on the November ballot
broomfield/2.summary: Council referred a lodging tax question to the November 3 ballot and passed resolutions supporting it and the Broomfield-Xcel franchise agreement.

broomfield/3.title: Affordable housing, Prop 123 and inclusionary housing
broomfield/3.summary: Council discussed opting into the next Prop 123 cycle with an expedited review for affordable housing, opted in, and heard a housing needs assessment update and the status of an inclusionary housing ordinance.

broomfield/4.title: Transit-oriented density rules and Front Range Passenger Rail
broomfield/4.summary: Council weighed how to comply with the state transit-oriented communities law requiring more density near transit and considered a rail station plan for Front Range Passenger Rail.

broomfield/5.title: Public hearings before cutting outdoor recreation facilities
broomfield/5.summary: Council passed a code change requiring a public hearing before a site plan amendment can reduce or eliminate outdoor recreation facilities.

broomfield/6.title: Chipotle at Palisade Park
broomfield/6.summary: The Land Use Review Commission and then council approved the plat and site plan for a Chipotle at Palisade Park, after a hearing that also touched on new parking ratios.

broomfield/7.title: Northlands PUD hospital and medical office heights
broomfield/7.summary: Council considered a Northlands PUD amendment changing building height and parking rules for hospital and medical office uses.

broomfield/8.title: Fiscal impact review for rezonings
broomfield/8.summary: Council adopted new criteria requiring a fiscal impact review for rezonings, PUD plans and special use reviews.

broomfield/9.title: Electric vehicle charging rules and fees
broomfield/9.summary: Council set fees for EV charging stations on city property and made EV charging a permitted use in non-residential districts.

broomfield/10.title: E-bike enforcement
broomfield/10.summary: Council introduced an ordinance on enforcing rules for electric bikes.

broomfield/11.title: Nordstrom Silo landmark nomination
broomfield/11.summary: Council considered designating the Nordstrom Silo as a local landmark.

broomfield/12.title: Enterprise utility ordinance
broomfield/12.summary: Council introduced an enterprise utility ordinance on first reading.

broomfield/13.title: Comprehensive plan and transportation mobility plan update
broomfield/13.summary: Staff briefed a city board on updating Broomfield's comprehensive plan and its transportation mobility plan, with housing affordability a central focus.

broomfield/14.title: Backyard setback variances in Red Leaf and Northmoor Estates
broomfield/14.summary: The Neighborhood Board of Adjustment approved homeowners' requests to shrink rear yard setbacks in Red Leaf and Northmoor Estates.

broomfield/15.title: Library strategic plan and flat 2027 budget
broomfield/15.summary: The library board reviewed its strategic plan and AI civics work and heard the 2027 library budget will be flat, raising worries about long-term erosion.

commerce-city/0.title: Data center moratorium and study session
commerce-city/0.summary: A council member asked for an ordinance placing a moratorium on data centers and council moved to schedule a study session, while the environmental policy commission researched data centers and drafted a recommendation for council.

commerce-city/1.title: Citywide legislative rezoning under the new land development code
commerce-city/1.summary: Council and the planning commission reviewed the legislative rezoning project that applies the 2025 land development code to the zoning map, then held a joint study session on Tier 2 code amendments to land uses and approval criteria.

commerce-city/2.title: Shamrock Foods heavy industrial rezoning at 52nd and Ivy
commerce-city/2.summary: Shamrock Foods asked to rezone its plant at 5199 Ivy Street from medium to heavy industrial and for a conditional use permit for food oil storage; the planning commission heard it and council's final hearing is set for November 16.
commerce-city/2.where: 5199 Ivy St, E 52nd Ave and Ivy St

commerce-city/3.title: Reunion Filing 39 subdivision near Chambers Road
commerce-city/3.summary: Oakwood Homes sought approval of an 84-lot final plat in the Reunion development near Chambers Road and Heartland Drive, drawing written public comment that the applicant responded to.
commerce-city/3.where: Reunion, Chambers Rd and Heartland Dr

commerce-city/4.title: Hogan property PUD amendment
commerce-city/4.summary: Council adopted a PUD amendment expanding the boundary and consolidating standards for 16.82 acres of the Hogan property near E 101st Way after a public hearing with written comment.

commerce-city/5.title: Annexations including Moreno Salas, Third Creek East and South Platte Crossing
commerce-city/5.summary: Council moved several annexations forward, including Moreno Salas at E 81st and Quebec, Third Creek East and South Platte Crossing Phase 2, and discussed annexing surrounded unincorporated enclaves.
commerce-city/5.where: E 81st Ave and Quebec St, Tower Rd, South Platte

commerce-city/6.title: 2027 city budget and improvement district budgets
commerce-city/6.summary: Council held preliminary budget sessions and a workshop and adopted the 2027 budget and tax levy, along with budgets and mill levies for the E-470 and Northern Infrastructure improvement districts and the urban renewal authority.

sources.body: E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District
E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District

commerce-city/7.title: Chambers Road widening
commerce-city/7.summary: Council awarded construction for Chambers Road improvements near Heartland Drive and heard a project update on the Chambers Road widening.

commerce-city/8.title: Oil and gas development north of the city
commerce-city/8.summary: Council members were invited to community open houses on the Cord oil and gas development plan and a Chevron proposal for wells north of the city.

sources.body: City Council Notice of Potential Quorum

commerce-city/9.title: Recreation and golf fee increases for 2027
commerce-city/9.summary: The parks commission supported proposed 2027 recreation and golf fee increases, which then went to council along with a fall review of the city's fees and charges.
commerce-city/9.where: Recreation centers, Buffalo Run golf course

commerce-city/10.title: Municipal noise ordinance
commerce-city/10.summary: Council discussed options and staff recommendations for updating the city's noise ordinance.

commerce-city/11.title: Municipal court jury trials and code enforcement changes
commerce-city/11.summary: Court staff presented code changes on jury trials and compliance and enforcement, which council then took up as ordinances.

commerce-city/12.title: Housing authority and affordable housing projects
commerce-city/12.summary: Council discussed the Commerce City Housing Authority and its list of current and completed affordable housing projects.

commerce-city/13.title: Public art for 96th Avenue, Second Creek Farm Park and police substation
commerce-city/13.summary: The arts commission chose artwork for 96th Avenue, Second Creek Farm Park and the golf course and discussed art for the police substation.

commerce-city/14.title: Trails and the Prairieways Action Plan
commerce-city/14.summary: The parks commission reviewed the city's trail system, future trails under the Prairieways Action Plan and how new development pays impact fees and dedicates parkland.

commerce-city/15.title: Police mobile command unit purchase
commerce-city/15.summary: Council approved budget changes to buy a mobile command unit for the police department from the fire district.

denver/0.title: Data center moratorium
denver/0.summary: City staff updated the Community Planning and Housing committee on Denver's moratorium on new data centers while the city works out rules for where they can go and how much power and water they can use.

denver/1.title: NWSL stadium at Santa Fe Yards and the Broadway Station bridge
denver/1.summary: Council amended the agreement with the Broadway Station metro district for the women's pro soccer stadium site and took a state grant for a pedestrian bridge over the rail lines linking the Broadway RTD station to the stadium and Santa Fe Yards.

denver/2.title: Mayor's proposed 2027 budget
denver/2.summary: The Finance Department walked council through the budget book, council worked through proposed changes to sales tax initiatives, and the mayor's 2027 budget was set for a public hearing on October 26.

sources.body: Operations Meeting of the City Council

denver/3.title: Denver Health sales tax spending
denver/3.summary: Council reviewed how the 0.34% Denver Health sales tax approved in 2024 is being spent and moved a string of new and amended contracts with Denver Health, including the behavioral health services at 777 Bannock Street.

denver/4.title: Homeless shelters and rapid rehousing contracts
denver/4.summary: Council approved a run of contracts for rapid resolution and rehousing, new emergency shelter at the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel on East Colfax, a safe outdoor space at 3815 N Steele Street and a micro-community shelter site.
denver/4.where: Sand & Sage Motel (East Colfax), 3815 N Steele St

denver/5.title: Downtown Development Authority boundaries and projects
denver/5.summary: Council repeatedly expanded the Denver Downtown Development Authority's boundaries and approved DDA funding for the Midland Condominiums, the University Building on 16th Street and 101 W Colfax, where the city is also leasing space.

denver/6.title: Council votes down Citibot and Slalom tech contracts
denver/6.summary: After being called out for debate, resolutions adding $3.9 million to the Citibot chatbot contract and $5 million to the Slalom consulting contract both failed on the council floor.

denver/7.title: Sunny Side Up city video contract
denver/7.summary: A contract for city marketing and recruiting videos drew pushback; an added $600,000 failed on the floor in August before a smaller $250,000 amendment came back in the fall.

denver/8.title: Affordable housing bonds and loans
denver/8.summary: Council approved housing revenue bonds for the Green Valley Vistas and Link and Pin apartments, a loan for 1600 Pearl, a loan for a 118-unit income-restricted building, and state money for middle-income row homes at Loretto Heights.
denver/8.where: Green Valley Ranch, North Capitol Hill, Loretto Heights

denver/9.title: Universal Recycling and Composting Ordinance rollout
denver/9.summary: Council heard an update on putting the recycling and composting ordinance into effect, which phases in recycling and compost service requirements for apartments and businesses.

denver/10.title: Flood control at the Globeville Levee, Sanderson Gulch and Harvard Gulch
denver/10.summary: Council moved agreements with the Mile High Flood District and federal grants for drainage and flood control work on the Globeville Levee from 31st Street to East 50th Avenue, along Sanderson Gulch and at Harvard Gulch.
denver/10.where: Globeville Levee, Sanderson Gulch, Harvard Gulch

denver/11.title: Airport expansion and airline leases at DIA
denver/11.summary: Council approved a $135 million project management contract for the North Terminal expansion, taxiway and gate apron construction, and new use-and-lease agreements with ten airlines.

denver/12.title: Rewrite of the city's minority and women-owned business contracting rules
denver/12.summary: Council passed a rewrite of the city code's minority-owned, women-owned and small business enterprise contracting program.

denver/13.title: Housing Stability's one-year plan for 2027
denver/13.summary: Council changed the code so the Department of Housing Stability can run on a one-year continuation plan for 2027 and bring a new long-range strategic plan in September 2027.

denver/14.title: Missing middle housing and zoning reform
denver/14.summary: Council toured missing middle housing as part of Unlocking Housing Choices and heard about regulatory reform and a federal PRO Housing grant meant to make more kinds of homes legal to build.

denver/15.title: West Colfax and Hazel Court rezonings
denver/15.summary: Council moved rezonings at 3418 W 14th Avenue and 1371 N Julian Street in West Colfax and held a public hearing on rezoning 76 N Hazel Court and nearby lots.
denver/15.where: 3418 W 14th Ave, 1371 N Julian St, 76 N Hazel Ct

denver/16.title: Traffic camera ordinance (AVIS)
denver/16.summary: Council worked on changes to the ordinance for the automated vehicle identification system, the city's photo traffic enforcement cameras.

denver/17.title: Council positions on Amendments 81 and 82
denver/17.summary: Council took up a proclamation opposing state ballot Amendment 81 on law enforcement and discussed Amendment 82 on a constitutional right to buy and sell natural gas.

denver/18.title: Limits on spending dedicated taxes on alcohol and perks
denver/18.summary: Council advanced bills barring Caring for Denver, Denver Preschool Program and college affordability tax money from being spent on alcohol, staff wellness programs and similar administrative costs.

denver/19.title: East Colfax sidewalk land acquisition
denver/19.summary: Council moved an ordinance letting the city buy or condemn land to add sidewalks where none exist along East Colfax in District 8.

denver/20.title: Entertainment license overhaul
denver/20.summary: Council updated the city code for entertainment licenses, including application and license fees.

denver/21.title: Filling an at-large council seat
denver/21.summary: A special meeting declared a vacancy in one of the two at-large council seats.

sources.body: Special Meeting Of The City Council

denver/22.title: ShotSpotter contract cut
denver/22.summary: Council cut about $147,000 from the SoundThinking (ShotSpotter) gunshot detection contract.

erie/0.title: Town mineral rights and the Draco oil and gas pad
erie/0.summary: After SM Energy backed out of buying town-owned mineral rights for its Draco drilling project, council repealed the sale ordinance and discussed whether to lease the minerals instead and what role the town should play in the state drilling permit process.

erie/1.title: New oil and gas rules and fees
erie/1.summary: The planning commission reviewed a rewrite of the town's oil and gas regulations covering per-well fees, legacy wells, noise, air quality, inspections and notification, with a resident urging higher inspection fees.

erie/2.title: 2027 budget cuts amid falling revenue
erie/2.summary: With sales tax growth under 2% and use tax and building permits down more than 40%, staff built a leaner 2027 budget with few new positions; advisory boards were told to cut their budgets, and hearings were set for October 27 and November 10.

erie/3.title: Page property open space rezoning
erie/3.summary: The open space board recommended rezoning land on the Page property west of the Cottonwood Extension Ditch as Reserved Open Space, which needs voter approval to ever sell or rezone, ahead of a council discussion set for November 10.
erie/3.where: Page property, near Reliance Park and CR 1.5

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/4.title: Protecting open space through zoning
erie/4.summary: The planning commission and open space board held a joint session on how open space is zoned, the Reserved Open Space district, the land acquisition strategy and how the open space board reviews development.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/5.title: Vista Ridge golf course and Vista Reserve development
erie/5.summary: The planning commission and council took up two amendments to the Vista Ridge planned development, including changes for the golf course and the Vista Reserve preliminary plat.

erie/6.title: Short-term rental rules
erie/6.summary: The planning commission and council held hearings on adding a short-term rental chapter to the town's development code.

erie/7.title: Erie Municipal Airport noise, hangars and fees
erie/7.summary: Residents complained about early-morning touch-and-go flights, while the airport board worked on hangar development, through-the-fence fees and a possible charter change to allow longer land leases, and council got a hangar development update.

erie/8.title: Hiring a new town manager
erie/8.summary: After 60 applications and interviews, council appointed Kelli Johnson as town manager starting January 4, 2027.

erie/9.title: Colliers Hill urban renewal tax increment
erie/9.summary: The urban renewal authority and council approved tax increment agreements for the Colliers Hill area, including a Weld County amendment that drops a requirement to spend some revenue on Weld County Road 5 and allows parks and recreation projects.

erie/10.title: Downtown Briggs Street redevelopment
erie/10.summary: The urban renewal authority paid for downtown infrastructure and design work and took up a development agreement for 150 Briggs Street, while council approved sidewalk patio licenses for businesses on Briggs Street.

erie/11.title: Erie Lake Dam seepage repairs
erie/11.summary: Council amended the design and construction contracts for the project to fix seepage at the Erie Lake dam.

erie/12.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
erie/12.summary: The town is asking the state to cut its Proposition 123 affordable housing requirement to 30 units, and planners discussed how the commitment will shape the development code update.

erie/13.title: Lodging tax and sales tax ballot measures
erie/13.summary: Two ballot measures are coming, a proposed 3.5% lodging tax tied to the Sundance Film Festival and a proposed sales tax increase.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/14.title: Coal Creek rezoning and stream restoration
erie/14.summary: The planning commission heard a rezoning of the Coal Creek property, and council authorized buying land for the County Line Road and Coal Creek stream restoration project.

erie/15.title: Water purchases and conservation
erie/15.summary: Council approved buying Colorado-Big Thompson water units, a home water audit program with Boulder County, and heard a presentation on Northern Water's NISP reservoir project.

erie/16.title: Flock cameras and security
erie/16.summary: Council met in executive session on security arrangements and Flock Safety license plate camera technology.

firestone/0.title: Comprehensive plan update
firestone/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on approving an update to Firestone's comprehensive plan.

firestone/1.title: Barefoot Lakes Filing 5 subdivision changes
firestone/1.summary: The planning commission recommended an amended preliminary plat for Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, with a neighbor raising concerns about views and buffering.

firestone/2.title: Parks and trails projects and 2027 budget requests
firestone/2.summary: The parks commission ranked trail fixes and new connections, including links toward St. Vrain State Park, rotted bridge boards south of Gateway Park and possible pickleball courts, as budget recommendations.

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/3.title: Town hall summer hours pilot
firestone/3.summary: Trustees discussed a pilot program for summer office hours.

frederick/0.title: Roads and Routes transportation sales tax ballot measure
frederick/0.summary: Trustees put a 1% transportation sales tax and related debt question on the November ballot to fund the Roads and Routes program, and discussed it at several meetings.

frederick/1.title: Land use code amendments and retail marijuana ban
frederick/1.summary: The planning commission and trustees worked through land use code amendments, including a ban on retail marijuana businesses.

frederick/2.title: Water resources and the Firestone water case
frederick/2.summary: Trustees discussed water supply issues, including opposing Firestone's water court case and treating a reservoir for phosphorus.

frederick/3.title: Public Works and Parks campus
frederick/3.summary: Trustees discussed plans for a new combined Public Works and Parks campus.

frederick/4.title: Historic preservation plan
frederick/4.summary: The town took up a historic preservation plan for its older buildings and downtown.

frederick/5.title: Public art murals and carvings
frederick/5.summary: The arts commission reviewed new murals and carvings for public spaces.

frederick/6.title: Youth commission work on mental health and bullying
frederick/6.summary: The youth commission focused on student mental health and bullying prevention.

frederick/7.title: Parks, open space and trails design standards
frederick/7.summary: The town reviewed new design standards for parks, open space and trails.

frederick/8.title: Wheatlands plat expiration and KO Industrial land
frederick/8.summary: Trustees dealt with the expiration of the Wheatlands plat and a land conveyance for the KO Industrial site.

frederick/9.title: 2027 budget
frederick/9.summary: The 2027 town budget was introduced to trustees.

glendale/0.title: Xcel franchise ballot question
glendale/0.summary: Council took up a resolution on ballot question 2B, which would grant Xcel Energy a new franchise in Glendale.

glendale/1.title: 2027 budget and tax levy
glendale/1.summary: Council introduced ordinances adopting the 2027 budget and setting the property tax levy, followed by a budget update.

glendale/2.title: Four Mile project
glendale/2.summary: Council met in executive session for legal advice on the Four Mile project.

glendale/3.title: Clubhouse entertainment liquor license
glendale/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on a new entertainment facility liquor license for a clubhouse on South Colorado Boulevard.

glendale/4.title: Community events planning
glendale/4.summary: Volunteer teams reported on the car show, Music on the Plaza and Get to Know Glendale events.

lafayette/0.title: New Land Use Code and citywide rezoning
lafayette/0.summary: Council passed the new Land Use Code and zoning map on first reading in August after a public hearing, then adopted it on second reading in September with amendments, after heavy testimony about housing diversity, parking, wildlife corridors and how the code follows the comprehensive plan.

lafayette/1.title: Old Town OTX-3 zoning and building heights on Public Road
lafayette/1.summary: Residents objected to the new OTX-3 zone allowing larger, taller buildings along Public Road south of Emma Street; a joint council and planning commission workshop agreed to shrink the maximum building footprint from 25,000 to 10,000 square feet and revisit height in a second ordinance.
lafayette/1.where: Public Road south of Emma St, Old Town

lafayette/2.title: Data center and advanced air mobility moratoriums
lafayette/2.summary: After council asked how the new code regulates data centers, it adopted an 18-month moratorium on land use applications and building permits for data centers in October, alongside an emergency 18-month moratorium on advanced air mobility facilities.

lafayette/3.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
lafayette/3.summary: Many residents urged council to end the Flock Safety license plate camera contract, and council weighed two versions of the 2027 budget, one with no Flock funding, and discussed a formal policy for automatic license plate readers.

lafayette/4.title: Naming the 701 S. Public Road pocket park for Rosebelle Lueras
lafayette/4.summary: Residents spoke at meeting after meeting asking that the new pocket park at 701 S. Public Road be named for Rosebelle Lueras, and council took up the naming in October.

lafayette/5.title: Zoning for churches along Highway 287
lafayette/5.summary: Church members raised concerns about how the new code zones churches, and council directed that the church parcels at Highway 287 and South Boulder Road be zoned like Immaculate Conception.

lafayette/6.title: Boulder Ranch development off Baseline and Burlington
lafayette/6.summary: Residents wrote in opposing the proposed high-density Boulder Ranch development on 78 acres near Baseline Road and Burlington, citing traffic, open space and the buffer agreement with Boulder, with over 2,000 petition signatures.

lafayette/7.title: LaMont Does Park and water park tax extension
lafayette/7.summary: Council put the extension of an expiring property tax for LaMont Does Park and the Great Outdoors Water Park on the November ballot, with residents speaking for and against.

lafayette/8.title: 2027 budget, fees and pay plan
lafayette/8.summary: Staff introduced a $128 million 2027 recommended budget, and council held a public hearing, adopted the budget and mill levy, amended fees and adopted the pay plan.

lafayette/9.title: Capital bond projects and general obligation bonds
lafayette/9.summary: Council authorized general obligation bonds for the voter-approved recreation center, service center and civic center projects and toured capital projects including the water treatment plant and West Baseline Road safety improvements.
lafayette/9.where: Bob L. Burger Recreation Center, Service Center, West Baseline Rd

lafayette/10.title: Douglass Elementary School closure concerns
lafayette/10.summary: Council directed staff to draft a letter asking the Boulder Valley School District to reconsider its process on Douglass Elementary's future after Lafayette families said they had no voice.

lafayette/11.title: Human Rights Board renamed and rescoped
lafayette/11.summary: Council adopted an ordinance changing the name, scope and duties of the Human Rights Board.

lafayette/12.title: Expedited review for affordable housing
lafayette/12.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting an expedited review policy for affordable housing projects.

lafayette/13.title: Street racing on South Public Road
lafayette/13.summary: An Avalon Flatirons resident complained about street racers gathering in a church parking lot off South Public Road.

longmont/0.title: Vance Brand Airport noise and future
longmont/0.summary: The city held a town hall on what it can legally do about airport noise, council heard a baseline report on voluntary noise abatement and options for airport noise monitoring, and held a vision session on the airport's future, governance and rebuilding trust with neighbors.
longmont/0.where: Vance Brand Municipal Airport, 229 Airport Rd

sources.body: Town Hall: What the City Can and Cannot Do About Airport Noise

longmont/1.title: Public safety tax increase on the November ballot
longmont/1.summary: Council chose between several versions of a sales and property tax increase to hire more police officers, dispatchers and firefighters, referred it to the November 3 ballot and urged voters to approve it.

longmont/2.title: Charter amendments on ranked choice voting and open space sales
longmont/2.summary: Council referred charter amendments to the November ballot to adopt ranked choice voting, change how council members are elected, and require voter approval to sell or convey open space.

longmont/3.title: 1st and Main urban renewal, transit center and parking garage
longmont/3.summary: Council approved the 1st and Main urban renewal plan and parking garage financing, a development agreement for the 1st and Main transit center and transit-oriented project, and the urban renewal authority signed tax increment agreements with the county, Northern Water, the school district and the DDA.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/4.title: 2027 budget and 2027-2031 capital program
longmont/4.summary: Staff presented the 2027 proposed budget and five-year capital improvement program, and council held two public hearings before giving final direction and setting the property tax levy.

longmont/5.title: Dry Creek, 8513 St. Vrain Road and Gateway Northwest annexations
longmont/5.summary: Council moved forward annexations and residential zoning for Dry Creek along Airport Road and Clover Basin Drive and 8513 St. Vrain Road, and the Longmont Gateway Northwest annexation at U.S. 287 and Park Ridge Avenue.
longmont/5.where: Airport Rd and Clover Basin Dr, 8513 St. Vrain Rd, US 287 and Park Ridge Ave

longmont/6.title: Trash, compost and sanitation rates
longmont/6.summary: Council discussed lining up waste rates with city policy goals and a possible subsidy for composting, and asked the Sustainability Advisory Board for feedback on the sanitation rate structure.

longmont/7.title: Water supply, drought and Ralph Price Reservoir
longmont/7.summary: The Water Board weighed a one-year water exchange with the St. Vrain and Left Hand Water Conservancy District, whose supply could run out by 2028 in continued drought, reviewed how Ralph Price Reservoir is managed, and heard about the Dry Creek Fire near Button Rock.
longmont/7.where: Button Rock Preserve / Ralph Price Reservoir

longmont/8.title: Affordable housing, inclusionary fee and expedited review
longmont/8.summary: Council set an expedited review process for affordable housing and adjusted the 2027 inclusionary housing fee-in-lieu, the housing board reviewed the 12% inclusionary requirement, and the housing authority reviewed the countywide affordable housing tax after two years.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with the Board of Education
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting
City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board

longmont/9.title: Human services funding hearings
longmont/9.summary: The Housing and Human Service Advisory Board set a scoring threshold and held weekly hearings with nonprofits applying for city human services funding.

longmont/10.title: Show cause hearing for 333 Main Street liquor license
longmont/10.summary: The licensing authority held a show cause hearing on a bar at 333 Main Street over rowdiness, noise, disturbances and open container violations.

sources.body: Local Licensing Authority- CONTINUED TO DATE TBD

longmont/11.title: Platte River Power and clean energy goals
longmont/11.summary: Platte River Power Authority told council and the Sustainability Advisory Board it cannot reach 100% noncarbon power by 2030 and is starting a new resource plan, and the board began work on the 2027 sustainability tax.

longmont/12.title: City flag redesign
longmont/12.summary: A selection panel and the Art in Public Places Commission worked through submissions for a new official Longmont flag.

sources.body: City of Longmont Official City Flag Redesign Selection Panel Meeting

longmont/13.title: Automated checkout workforce impact fee
longmont/13.summary: Council members discussed a possible fee on stores that replace cashiers with automated checkout.

longmont/14.title: Copper Peak development at 2704 Main Street
longmont/14.summary: Council considered a concept plan amendment for the Copper Peak development on part of the Wal-Mart retail center at 2704 Main Street.

longmont/15.title: Contractor's shops in mixed-use employment zones
longmont/15.summary: The planning commission took up a resident-initiated code change to allow contractor's shops in the MU-E zone district, with the hearing continued to November 18.

longmont/16.title: New homes at 10930 Airport Road
longmont/16.summary: A neighborhood meeting covered a proposal for new single-family homes at 10930 Airport Road that would need a comprehensive plan amendment, rezoning and subdivision.

longmont/17.title: Avis car rental at 206 S. Main Street
longmont/17.summary: A neighborhood meeting covered Avis's plan to open a rental office at 206 S. Main Street and store cars behind it, a conditional use next to a greenway that council must decide.

longmont/18.title: School safety, housing and growth with St. Vrain Valley Schools
longmont/18.summary: At a joint meeting with the Board of Education, council discussed safe street crossings for students, shared housing efforts and how much say the city has over single-family versus apartment development.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with the Board of Education

longmont/19.title: Front Range Passenger Rail
longmont/19.summary: The urban renewal authority considered a letter of support for Front Range Passenger Rail.

longmont/20.title: Property tax burden
longmont/20.summary: At its legislative dinner, council raised the gap between the property taxes residents pay and what cities receive.

louisville/0.title: Inclusionary housing ordinance update
louisville/0.summary: Council rewrote the inclusionary housing rules that require affordable units in new development, drawing letters from Strong Towns Louisville and residents asking for small-project exemptions and by-right incentives, before a final hearing in September.

louisville/1.title: Golf course fees and the Coal Creek Golf Fund deficit
louisville/1.summary: With the golf fund's costs projected to outrun green fees, the recreation board modeled fee increases, heard golfers worried about losing the course's community culture, and sent 2027 fee and pass recommendations to council.

louisville/2.title: 2027-2028 budget and operating deficit
louisville/2.summary: Council worked through a "transitionary" budget with costs growing faster than revenue, an operating deficit, service level cuts such as cancelled event sponsorships, a refined six-year capital plan, and a final budget hearing on October 20.

louisville/3.title: Centennial Valley residential development plan
louisville/3.summary: Council and its boards held hearings on amending the Centennial Valley general development plan to allow housing that could grow Louisville's housing by 12%, with residents arguing the parks, trails and open space in the plan are too small.

louisville/4.title: AdventHealth hospital and helipad at Redtail Ridge
louisville/4.summary: Council took up the planned development and a special review use for a helicopter pad at the AdventHealth (Avista) hospital at Redtail Ridge, with questions about exemptions from LEED and solar requirements.

louisville/5.title: Delo Boom 135-unit development
louisville/5.summary: The planning commission reviewed the final plans for 135 homes and a small commercial space at 1390 Cannon Street and 1301 Courtesy Road, with supporters citing the need for attainable housing and a Delo resident warning of a parking shortfall.

louisville/6.title: Open space, parks and trails long-range plan
louisville/6.summary: Boards and council reviewed the draft PROS guidebook and trails plan, with the open space group LOSA objecting to land classifications and trails it says conflict with the city charter's open space protections.

louisville/7.title: Sustainability funding, bag tax and electrification rebates
louisville/7.summary: The sustainability board and council discussed a sustainability tax, renegotiating the Xcel franchise, using bag tax money, water conservation in a snowmelt-dependent system and new home electrification and heat pump rebates.

louisville/8.title: Marshall Fire five-year remembrance
louisville/8.summary: Council reviewed survey results on a Marshall Fire five-year remembrance, with remembrance funds going toward Superior's memorial project.

louisville/9.title: Fire Smart Louisville wildfire program
louisville/9.summary: Council funded Fire Smart Louisville, a volunteer effort with the Boulder Watershed Collective to help neighborhoods reduce wildfire risk, and approved a $100,000 agreement with the collective.

louisville/10.title: Comprehensive plan and development code update
louisville/10.summary: The planning commission reviewed the new comprehensive plan's growth projections and the city launched a development code rewrite with state grant money, as residents raised concerns about growth, traffic, water, wildfire evacuation and community character.

louisville/11.title: Affordable housing strategy and Prop 123
louisville/11.summary: Council heard a housing strategic framework from Trestle Strategy Group, reviewed a concept for affordable senior housing on Centennial Drive, and set expedited review for affordable projects and a state Prop 123 commitment.

louisville/12.title: Historic preservation tax ballot measure and landmarks
louisville/12.summary: Council took a position on the November historic preservation tax measure and designated landmarks including the Caranci House at 1101 Main and the Giorzelli House, with grants for the James House, Mudrock House and the grain elevator at 540 County Road.
louisville/12.where: 1101 Main St, 700 Pine St, 613 Grant Ave, 741 Jefferson Ave

louisville/13.title: Grain Elevator and Grain Yard redevelopment
louisville/13.summary: The Revitalization Commission worked on a tax increment financing agreement for the Grain Elevator and facade and property improvement grants for the Grain Yard.

louisville/14.title: Front and Center construction impacts downtown
louisville/14.summary: Business owners raised worries that the Front and Center construction project will hurt Street Fair and Front Street businesses, and commissioners discussed construction impact support grants.

louisville/15.title: Trash, recycling and compost rate increases
louisville/15.summary: Council set new refuse, recycling and compost collection fees effective September 1, with questions about why recycling and compost rates rose.

louisville/16.title: Utility rates for 2027
louisville/16.summary: A revised 2027 water and sewer rate presentation was delayed and then discussed, and the northeast water loop project was pulled from the budget after rate talks.

louisville/17.title: Business incentives for Infleqtion and Arsenal Health
louisville/17.summary: Council approved business assistance agreements worth $281,114 for Infleqtion Quantum and $208,400 for Arsenal Health.

louisville/18.title: City land deals at Empire Road, 1155 Pine Street and Gateway open space
louisville/18.summary: Council approved buying land at 1501 Empire Road, extended a lease-purchase at 1155 Pine Street, and approved buying the Gateway open space property.
louisville/18.where: 1501 Empire Rd, 1155 Pine St, Gateway open space

louisville/19.title: Bocce court and Community Park upkeep
louisville/19.summary: Residents asked for better upkeep of the bocce courts at Memory Square and Community Park, and boards pushed for shade structures and flower bed improvements at Community Park.

louisville/20.title: Prairie dogs on open space
louisville/20.summary: Residents asked the open space board to deal with prairie dogs moving into neighborhoods near open space.

lyons/0.title: Planet Bluegrass annexation on North St. Vrain Drive
lyons/0.summary: Planet Bluegrass asked the town to annex and give PUD zoning to two parcels at 19617 and 19661 North St. Vrain Drive near Eagle Canyon, and the utilities, economic vitality, parks and trustee boards reviewed the referral ahead of a trustee hearing.

lyons/1.title: 2nd and 3rd Avenue stormwater and sidewalk projects
lyons/1.summary: After a federal BRIC grant was denied, trustees weighed a $3.8 million loan or bond for the 2nd and 3rd Avenue stormwater and sidewalk work, learned a public vote is needed, and moved ahead with a Safe Routes to School sidewalk grant.

lyons/2.title: Wildfire mitigation and new fire-resistant roof rules
lyons/2.summary: Trustees discussed wildfire mitigation strategies and costs, held a town hall on fire risk, and set mid-roof inspection fees as the town moved to the state fire code requiring fire-resistant roofs after a hailstorm.

lyons/3.title: Electric rate increase and time-of-use rates
lyons/3.summary: The utilities board worked out a roughly 9% electric rate increase for 2027 after transmission costs jumped, while local businesses raised concerns that the new time-of-use electricity rates were rolled out without consulting them.

lyons/4.title: Strategic growth and water supply element of the comprehensive plan
lyons/4.summary: Boards and trustees reviewed a new strategic growth and water supply element required by state law SB24-174, which found the town has enough water for the 87 housing units the regional needs assessment suggests.

lyons/5.title: Wastewater treatment plant upgrades
lyons/5.summary: Trustees heard the 60% design update for wastewater treatment plant improvements, a separate $5.8 million need with a federal grant pending, and the utilities board reviewed proposed equipment changes awaiting state approval.

lyons/6.title: 2027 budget and supplemental 2026 spending
lyons/6.summary: Trustees held budget workshops on 2026 supplemental items and the 2027 budget and five-year capital plan, informed by a resident budget survey, with infrastructure as the top priority.

lyons/7.title: Automatic license plate readers
lyons/7.summary: Trustees discussed automatic license plate reader programs and a proposed Flock Safety agreement.

lyons/8.title: Special event and park use fee waivers
lyons/8.summary: Trustees and the parks and economic vitality commissions worked on a policy for waiving special event and park use fees for local versus outside groups.

lyons/9.title: Special event lodging for the Sundance Film Festival
lyons/9.summary: A task force followed up on the new special event lodging ordinance letting RVs and temporary lodging serve festival visitors, and shifted its Sundance plans toward private events and curated outdoor experiences.

lyons/10.title: Downtown Vacant to Vibrant incentive program
lyons/10.summary: The economic vitality commission designed a sliding-scale incentive program to fill vacant downtown storefronts.

lyons/11.title: Water rights cash in lieu for 402 Main Street
lyons/11.summary: Roots to Revival asked to use a Lake McIntosh water share and pay cash in lieu for the rest of its water rights dedication at 402 Main Street, which trustees ratified, alongside a broader look at the cash-in-lieu policy.

lyons/12.title: Streetlight LED upgrades
lyons/12.summary: Trustees awarded a contract to convert streetlights to LEDs after the utilities board trimmed the project to lights outside CDOT's Main Street right-of-way to cut the bid roughly in half.

lyons/13.title: Moss Rock hotel and Main Street redevelopment
lyons/13.summary: The urban renewal authority reviewed the Moss Rock hotel project at 343-347 Main Street and a reimbursement agreement for Roots to Revival at 402 Main Street, and adopted its 2027 budget.

lyons/14.title: Affordable housing at Carter Court and Seward Street
lyons/14.summary: The Boulder County Housing Authority updated trustees on affordable housing projects at Carter Court and Seward Street, and the town opted into Prop 123.

lyons/15.title: Variance at 441 Stickney Street
lyons/15.summary: The board of adjustment held a hearing on a corner side setback variance at 441 Stickney Street that drew public comment.

mead/0.title: Twelve-month moratorium on data centers
mead/0.summary: The Board of Trustees adopted a twelve-month moratorium on data centers on August 31, and staff told the planning commission the town has not yet received any data center proposals.

mead/1.title: Waterfront Filing No. 2 mixed-use development
mead/1.summary: The planning commission recommended conditional approval of the Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat, focusing on traffic capacity, road improvements and trail connections, and called for coordinating transportation across nearby developments.

mead/2.title: 2027 budget and improvement district budgets
mead/2.summary: The 2027 proposed budget was presented to trustees, along with budgets and mill levies for the Highway 66 and I-25 and Elevation 25 improvement districts and the urban renewal authority.

mead/3.title: Urban renewal tax increment incentive policy
mead/3.summary: The Mead Urban Renewal Authority took up a formal policy for judging developer requests for tax increment reimbursement, based on financial need, projected tax revenue and extraordinary costs.

mead/4.title: Annexations and public facilities zoning
mead/4.summary: The planning commission recommended zoning for the town-owned Valdez annexation and 1785 Weld County Road 32, public facilities zoning for other town land, and the Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat.

mead/5.title: I-25 sewer relocation and Safe Routes to School
mead/5.summary: Trustees awarded construction contracts for the I-25 sewer relocation and the Mead Safe Routes to School project.

mead/6.title: High Plains Boulevard, new library and police facility
mead/6.summary: The town marked the near-finished High Plains Boulevard expansion between WCR 32 and 36, accepted improvements for the new High Plains Library District branch, and broke ground on a new police facility in Liberty Ranch.
mead/6.where: High Plains Blvd, Liberty Ranch, Chaparral St

nederland/0.title: Rezoning 242 and 252 E 5th Street for A-frame homes
nederland/0.summary: The planning commission recommended rezoning two steep commercial lots on East 5th Street to medium density residential for two A-frame homes, after a neighbor worried about losing commercial zoning flexibility and another resident spoke in support.

nederland/1.title: Outdoor dining and sales rules
nederland/1.summary: The town moved to allow outdoor sales, eating and drinking in its zoning use table, with safety standards near roadways.

nederland/2.title: Temporary use permits
nederland/2.summary: The planning commission and trustees worked on Ordinance 893 for staff-approved temporary use permits of up to 90 days that staff can revoke over safety problems.

nederland/3.title: Flex zoning for housing and redevelopment
nederland/3.summary: The planning commission began discussing flex zoning to allow more housing types and mixed uses, including in the Wolf Tongue industrial area and near East Street Garage.

nederland/4.title: Parks, open space and trails master plan
nederland/4.summary: The parks board finished revisions to the parks, recreation, open space and trails plan for trustees to review, and kept planning a replacement for the Chipeta Park playground.

sources.body: PROSAB - Nederland Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Advisory Board

nederland/5.title: Merging the zoning adjustment board into the planning commission
nederland/5.summary: The town moved an ordinance to dissolve its Board of Zoning Adjustment and hand its variance work to the planning commission, citing few applications and trouble filling the volunteer board.

nederland/6.title: Safer Main Streets crosswalk and sidewalk project
nederland/6.summary: Trustees approved an engineering agreement for crosswalk and sidewalk improvements under the Safer Main Streets program, and backed the fire district's wildfire mitigation grant.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance and five-year anniversary
superior/0.summary: The town is designing a Marshall Fire Remembrance with a gathering place and pet memorial, setting up fundraising through Colorado Gives with $25,000 committed by Louisville, and planning a five-year anniversary resilience celebration on December 18.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/1.title: 2027 budget and property tax levy
superior/1.summary: Council held a series of budget review sessions on the 2027 budget and five-year plan, with sales tax flat and vehicle use tax down, then set a public hearing to adopt the budget, fees and property tax levy along with the metro district and urban renewal budgets.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property development at 7500 S 88th Street
superior/2.summary: Garrett Companies sought a 25th amendment to the Rock Creek Ranch planned development for the Zaharias property, with residents speaking at the planning commission hearing before it went to council.

superior/3.title: Pirate Park playground renovation
superior/3.summary: Council approved a design-build contract with Altitude Recreation to rebuild the Pirate Park playground, and the parks committee and council got regular progress updates.

superior/4.title: Water conservation and turf reduction
superior/4.summary: The town drafted a waterwise landscape roadmap and a tool for ranking non-functional turf to remove, gathered resident input on Shape Superior, and amended its Northern Water supply allotment.

superior/5.title: Prairie dog and wildlife management plans
superior/5.summary: The open space committee worked on a prairie dog management plan covering relocation and conflicts, a broader town wildlife plan, and balancing wildfire mitigation with habitat.

superior/6.title: Coyote Ridge trail recommendations
superior/6.summary: A consultant presented recommended trail projects for Coyote Ridge open space, to be priced and scheduled once staff sign off.

superior/7.title: Adopting the 2024 International Fire Code
superior/7.summary: Council adopted the 2024 International Fire Code after a hearing continued from August, with the Mountain View Fire Protection District presenting.

superior/8.title: Boulder County early childhood mill levy
superior/8.summary: Council passed a resolution supporting the Boulder County ballot measure to raise the property tax for early childhood care and education, after discussing the county's child care investment initiative.

superior/9.title: 88th Street bike and pedestrian improvements
superior/9.summary: Council approved an agreement with CDOT for bicycle and pedestrian improvements along 88th Street.

superior/10.title: Trash, recycling and electric garbage trucks
superior/10.summary: Republic Services briefed council on contamination, blocked containers and its electric collection trucks, as the town looks at a future single-hauler contract and apartment recycling and composting.

superior/11.title: Rock Creek Parkway, Community Center and pool construction
superior/11.summary: Council received construction updates on Rock Creek Parkway, the community center and the north and south pools.
superior/11.where: Rock Creek Parkway, Superior Community Center

thornton/0.title: Data center moratorium
thornton/0.summary: Council held two discussions in late August and early September on whether to adopt a moratorium on data centers, with a staff presentation on data center impacts.

thornton/1.title: 2027 budget recommendation
thornton/1.summary: Council worked through the city manager's recommended 2027 budget over several planning sessions and meetings this fall.

thornton/2.title: 2027 utility rates
thornton/2.summary: Council reviewed proposed water, sewer and other utility rate changes for 2027.

thornton/3.title: Creekside Gardens annexation at 140th and Washington
thornton/3.summary: Council considered annexing and zoning the Creekside Gardens property near 140th Avenue and Washington Street.

thornton/4.title: Welby Station rezoning at 88th and Welby
thornton/4.summary: Council took up zoning for the Welby Station development near 88th Avenue and Welby Road.

thornton/5.title: Bellflower annexation at 140th and Holly
thornton/5.summary: Council considered the Bellflower annexation and zoning near 140th Avenue and Holly Street.

thornton/6.title: Parks and arts master plans
thornton/6.summary: Council reviewed updates to the parks master plan and the arts and culture master plan.

thornton/7.title: Station area plans for York at 144th and North Thornton
thornton/7.summary: Council looked at station area plans around future transit stops at York Street and 144th Avenue and at North Thornton near State Highway 7.

thornton/8.title: Thornton Parkway multimodal path
thornton/8.summary: Council took up a multimodal path project along Thornton Parkway.

thornton/9.title: Municipal fine and fee schedule
thornton/9.summary: Council reviewed a new municipal fine and fee schedule, including results of a fee survey and staff recommendations.

thornton/10.title: City code changes after a Supreme Court ruling
thornton/10.summary: Council considered amending city code to bring it in line with a recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling.

thornton/11.title: Liquor license hearings at First Street Plaza
thornton/11.summary: Council held liquor license hearings, including one at First Street Plaza where neighbors filed opposition.

thornton/12.title: Water revenue bonds
thornton/12.summary: Council considered issuing water revenue bonds to fund water system projects.

thornton/13.title: Residential housing design standards
thornton/13.summary: Council reviewed changes to design standards for new residential housing.
